title: The D Question, Answered in G
motif_identity: A memorable 4/4 sentence begins on D5 for one beat, leaps up a fourth to G5 then steps A5 in paired eighths, rises to B5 for one beat, and falls to A5 for one beat. Its continuation turns down through F-sharp–E–F-sharp in a one-beat plus paired-eighth rhythm before G5–D5 complete the dominant-bound question. The answer begins lower with B4–D5 as paired eighths, rises to G5 for a beat, and later reshapes the descent into C5–B4 paired eighths and A4 before climbing D5–F-sharp5 to the final G5. The identity is therefore the leap, paired quick steps, one-beat crest, and answering descent/recovery—not an isolated scale fragment.
harmonic_debt: Section 2 ends on V7 of G after its E-minor diversion. Section 3 resolves that debt at once, then creates one last cadential V7 only to be discharged by the final G-major section.
resolution_intent: A final G-major authentic cadence supports a melodic G that is held as the actual endpoint; no new dominant or diversion follows.

narrative_acts.cause: The opening leap needs a destination commensurate with its confidence.
narrative_acts.consequence: Its first phrase settles on dominant D, making the second phrase necessary.
narrative_acts.unresolved: Whether the ascent can be stable rather than merely rhetorical.
narrative_acts.resolution_target: A first authentic G arrival after the D question.

narrative_acts.cause: The first answer has exposed a descending tail that can speak independently.
narrative_acts.consequence: A lower reply leads through A7 to E minor and leaves V7 of G unpaid.
narrative_acts.unresolved: The tonic has been deferred after the E-minor diversion.
narrative_acts.resolution_target: Resolve the held dominant from the continuation into a transformed G-major return.

narrative_acts.section: Transformation and climax: ascent against descent
narrative_acts.cause: The delayed dominant and opposing melodic directions demand simultaneous resolution.
narrative_acts.consequence: The original contour answers on G at its greatest register and coordinated harmonic force.
narrative_acts.unresolved: The answer has occurred, but still needs proportionate repose.
narrative_acts.resolution_target: A final reduced restatement after the climactic G arrival.

narrative_acts.cause: The climax has paid the dominant debt and clarified the protagonist's destination.
narrative_acts.consequence: The sentence returns without argument and ends on G.
narrative_acts.resolution_target: Sustained sounding G as final melodic and harmonic degree.

chord_palette.label: A dominant seventh, applied dominant of E minor

sections.name: Premise: the answered question
sections.function: Establish the complete melodic sentence and prove that its dominant question has an answer.
sections.harmonic_direction: G tonic is tested by a real half cadence at bar 4, then recovered through B-bass tonic, IV, and cadential six-four.
sections.motif_treatment: Present the complete eight-bar sentence exactly as established: the rising leap and short-long continuation ask on D, then the lower continuation regains height and closes on G.

sections.name: Continuation: the lower reply
sections.function: Develop the sentence into dialogue and leave the original tonic answer temporarily unpaid.
sections.harmonic_direction: A brief applied dominant A7 introduces C-sharp only for its exact window; C-sharp resolves down by whole step to B in E minor. E minor becomes a meaningful but non-final resting place.
sections.motif_treatment: The opening ascent is sequenced one degree lower, then an autonomous answering line enters with the descent in longer values. The original cadence is delayed: the two thoughts meet on a quiet E-minor rather than G.

harmonic_events.purpose: retain shared G anchor while the sequel begins
functional chromatic push; C-sharp must resolve to B next
autonomous reply lands on B-bearing E minor
withhold G by stopping on its dominant

sections.name: Transformation and climax: ascent against descent
sections.function: Make the original question and its answer simultaneously audible at a scale that exceeds the final release.
sections.harmonic_direction: The delayed V from the continuation is paid at the opening G, but that tonic is destabilized toward C through G7. IV–ii7–Cad64–V7 rebuild the original cadential logic at greater span and intensity, arriving on G before the final section.
sections.motif_treatment: Transform the protagonist: its initial leap is compressed into urgent paired entries, while the former descending reply rises against it. At the peak, the full original contour returns at expanded register and is answered immediately, not postponed.

harmonic_events.purpose: tonic is made transitional rather than final
broad color contrast, still tied to G by common tones
climactic return of the original question over cadential six-four
audible climax answer: original contour now reaches stable G
release begins by letting tonic change bass relation
final approach is announced, not abruptly pasted on

sections.name: Resolution: the sentence at rest
sections.function: Confirm that the opening dominant question, the minor diversion, and the climactic expansion all resolve to the same G-major home.
sections.harmonic_direction: The final dominant resolves immediately to G. A B-bass inversion and IV recall the earlier answer without reopening the question; cadential six-four and V7 receive one final, proportionate tonic resolution.
sections.motif_treatment: Reduce to the protagonist alone: its opening leap is now calm and metrically clear, its descent is shortened, and its final G is sustained as a completed consequence rather than a cue for more development.

harmonic_events.purpose: last recollection of the question, now clearly finite
sounding final G; melody must finish on G
